Maxon Plus Adds AI to Generate 3D Models + Blender 5.3 Launches | Motion Mondays

Maxon Plus turns text prompts and reference images into 3D base meshes with AI, Blender 5.3 renders Gaussian splats natively, and Figma’s new beta lets you animate design layers in 3D.

By School of Motion1 min read

This week: Maxon Plus introduces AI tools for models and textures, and Maxon Review lets clients pin feedback directly onto a 3D model. Blender 5.3 lets you bring a scan of a real location into a scene and fly a camera through it. Figma’s 3D transforms beta adds depth and perspective to editable design layers. We’ll also check out Kyle Hamrick’s After Effects tips, TerrainStudio’s aligned map exports, and Caddis’s new 3D workspace and After Effects integration.

Also this week: Affinity brings its free design app to iPad, All Flows returns in May, and SDF Builder gives Cinema 4D artists a new way to blend shapes. We’ll check out work from André Dias, Imaginary Forces, and BUCK Sydney, plus Chris Chatel’s WOW Factory project in our Student of the Week spotlight. And from School of Motion: Figma Design for Motion is out, our Black Friday sale starts November 27, and we have a full December events calendar.

New course: Figma Design for Motion

Turn a client brief into artwork built for animation.

By School of Motion2 min readOv

Build the design before you build the motion. In Figma Design for Motion, Bekki Leahy takes you from a client brief to moodboards, illustrated storyboards, and reusable design systems in Figma.

The beginner course includes 10+ hours of recorded lessons and four hands-on projects: a moodboard, a five-frame storyboard, a sticker pack, and a modular festival campaign with a style guide.

EXPLORE FIGMA DESIGN FOR MOTION

How do I get the course?

All-Access members: once the course is released, look for Figma Design for Motion in your training library.

New to All-Access? Explore membership to see how course access, project feedback, and the School of Motion community fit your learning plans.

JOIN ALL-ACCESS

Who is this course for?

This course is for motion designers and illustrators who want to develop visual ideas in Figma, not just collect another tool. It starts with files, pages, frames, and the interface before moving into vector illustration, components, and a modular campaign.

Figma Design is the main tool. The setup lesson covers the free Starter plan and recommends the desktop app. After Effects is used for animation handoff, so familiarity with it will help with that part of the workflow.

The course compares SVG and Overlord handoffs, including what needs preparation or troubleshooting. It is about making artwork ready for animation, not assuming every effect will arrive unchanged.

What will I learn?

  • Organize Figma files, pages, and frames for visual research and presentations

  • Translate a brief into a moodboard with references, typography, masks, and a clear visual direction

  • Develop rough thumbnails into a five-frame illustrated storyboard with editable vector artwork

  • Use palettes, textures, masks, and layer organization with animation handoff in mind

  • Prepare artwork for After Effects and compare SVG with the Overlord workflow

  • Build a coordinated sticker pack using geometry, gradients, type, and shared styles

  • Create components and variants so a design can change without rebuilding every asset

  • Build a modular festival campaign and document its rules in a usable style guide

For a wider view of the process, read A Guide to Completing Your Motion Design Project. It connects moodboards and storyboards to the later production decisions they support.

EXPLORE FIGMA DESIGN FOR MOTION

Black Friday 2026 Deals For Motion Designers

Explore Black Friday 2026 offers for motion designers, from animation software and plugins to sound libraries and School of Motion annual All-Access.

By School of Motion16 min readV-

Black Friday is a good time to buy the tools you'll actually use, not a second career managing subscriptions. We've rounded up verified offers for motion designers, including animation software, creative plugins, and sound libraries. Some deals are live; others have announced start dates. Check the dates, plan, and fine print before you buy.

Deal Index

School Of Motion: School of Motion All-Access

Software And Creative Assets: Adobe · aescripts + aeplugins · ProtoPie · INSYDIUM · BOOM Library · Greyscalegorilla + KitBash3D · Chaos · Beeble.ai · True Grit Texture Supply · Fab · ActionVFX · Motion Ape · Krotos · Topaz Labs · Sonniss · A Sound Effect · ElevenLabs · Clam Sync · FX Elements · Toolfarm · HDRI Hub · Caddis · Blendkit · Kstudio · Spline Dynamics · RUVAU · Soundtoys · Render Camp · The Pixel Lab · Reallusion · Soft8Soft: Verge3D · Magic Automa AI · iMeshh · StormVFX: HydroFX · Next Limit · 3DModels.org

Hardware: Huion Kamvas 13 (Gen 3) · Huion Kamvas 16 (Gen 3) · MSI Vector 16 HX AI · HP HyperX OMEN MAX 45L · ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 XT · PNY GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Overclocked · Wacom

Miscellaneous: UPLIFT V3 Essential Standing Desk · Elgato Stream Deck MK.2 · Huanuo Monitor Arm With Laptop Tray · Logitech MX Master 3S

FEATURED OFFER | SCHOOL OF MOTION

Build Your Skills For Less: 25% Off Annual All-Access

A new plugin can speed up a task. Knowing what to do with it is the bigger upgrade. Our Black Friday sale takes 25% off the first year of an annual All-Access subscription, giving you every School of Motion course for one price. Pick the skills you want to sharpen, explore something outside your usual toolkit, and make your next project the reason to learn it.

Black Friday sale details

Starts November 27, 2026 at 9 AM ET. Ends December 2, 2026 at 5 PM ET.

Use code 25OFF at checkout when the sale begins.

First-time annual subscribers only. Previous annual All-Access subscribers are not eligible. Discount applies to the first year only. For team training, connect with our sales team.

Explore Our Black Friday Offer

More Verified Deals For Motion Designers

Adobe

Creative Cloud Pro: US$29.99/month for the first year, annual plan billed monthly.

If your day jumps between After Effects, Premiere Pro, Photoshop, and Illustrator, this is the big software bill to look at first. Creative Cloud Pro puts those apps in one subscription. The first-year price is aimed at new subscribers, though, so don't mistake it for a renewal discount on the account you're already using.

View Adobe’s Black Friday Offer

For eligible first-time individual subscribers buying directly from Adobe. Requires a 12-month commitment; renews at the then-current price, currently US$69.99/month. Education, OEM, and volume licensing excluded.

Offer & terms

aescripts + aeplugins

25% off everything*

You know that little task you repeat 80 times a day? There's a decent chance someone has built a tool for it. aescripts' sale covers plugins, scripts, and workflow helpers for animation, editing, and 3D work. Start with the tools you've tested and know you'll use. A crowded Extensions menu is not, by itself, a workflow upgrade.

Shop aescripts Deals

Exclusions include Stardust, Templater, The Power of Expression books, gift cards, and some order types. Subscription discounts cover the first term only; some products differ and discounts may not stack. Check the sale page for checkout instructions.

Offer & terms · Brand announcement

ProtoPie

40% off Pro Yearly

A UI animation looks great in a reel. A prototype that responds when someone actually taps it is a different kind of useful. ProtoPie lets motion designers explore interaction, timing, and transitions in working prototypes for screens and connected devices. It's worth a look if your projects sit between motion design, product design, and UX.

Get ProtoPie’s Pro Yearly Offer

For new subscribers on Pro Yearly, not every plan. Paid Connect Core and User Testing add-ons also receive 40% off at checkout. Check the renewal price before subscribing.

Offer & terms · Brand announcement

INSYDIUM

50% off everything

For 3D artists who want to get deeper into particles, simulation, and procedural work, INSYDIUM is a particularly relevant stop. The sale includes tools such as NeXus for Cinema 4D and Blender. Think of it as a chance to pick up the systems behind more ambitious effects, not a promise that the next simulation will art-direct itself.

Shop INSYDIUM’s Black Friday Sale

Enter the code at checkout. Prices exclude VAT; offers cannot be combined. Maintenance and upgrades require an account. Check subscription renewal pricing separately.

Offer & terms · Brand announcement

BOOM Library

Buy two products, get the lowest-priced third product free.

The animation isn't finished just because the render is done. A well-placed impact, movement sound, or bit of atmosphere can make the same sequence feel much more intentional. BOOM's three-for-two offer is a useful way to build a sound-effects kit around the work you actually make, rather than hunting for one more placeholder whoosh at delivery time.

Explore BOOM’s Black November Deals

The lowest-priced item in each group of three is free, applied at checkout. Prices exclude VAT. No sale-wide end date is listed; the prize-draw deadline is separate.

Offer & terms

Greyscalegorilla + KitBash3D

40% off annual plans during Cyber Month.

When a 3D scene needs better surfaces or lighting, you don’t always need another afternoon building everything from scratch. Greyscalegorilla gives you materials, HDRIs, textures, models, and Cinema 4D tools to dress and light your next style frame or animation. Need the world around your hero object, too? The Everything Bundle adds KitBash3D’s environments, buildings, props, and vehicles inside Cargo. Choose the library you’ll actually use, then put those assets to work.

Shop Greyscalegorilla’s Cyber Month Sale

The sale page advertises 40% off all annual plans, including the Everything Bundle. Monthly plans are not included in this offer. No sale deadline or discounted renewal terms are listed; existing-subscriber eligibility is not stated. Individual plans are for one artist; studios should check Teams licensing.

Offer & terms

Chaos

20% off new annual Enscape, V-Ray, Corona and Veras plans.

If your motion work includes product visualization, architectural animation, or rendered environments, check the eligible Chaos plans. The early-access offer covers annual plans for Enscape, V-Ray, Corona, and Veras. Pick the tool that fits your existing pipeline; a render-engine discount is less exciting if it also means rebuilding your workflow from scratch.

Explore Chaos’s Annual Plan Offers

New annual licenses are the confirmed eligibility. Discount is applied in the cart; no code required. Check the exact product and renewal price. No end date is listed.

Offer & terms

Beeble.ai

30% off the first year of yearly Cloud plans; 20% off the first month for new monthly customers.

For motion designers mixing live action, compositing, and AI-assisted video, Beeble Cloud brings relighting, background work, and other VFX tools into a node-based canvas. The sale is an opportunity to test where it fits in your process, not just collect another generator. Compare the credit allowance with the kind of shots you expect to make.

Explore Beeble’s Cloud Plan Offers

Cloud plans only. Yearly discount covers the first year; monthly discount covers the first month for first-time paying customers. Annual plans renew at regular price. Studio desktop and API access are separate; subscription credits do not roll over.

Offer & terms · Brand announcement

True Grit Texture Supply

50–70% off sitewide.

Sometimes the thing your design needs is less polish, not more. True Grit's brushes, paper textures, halftones, and effects help give clean digital artwork a more tactile character. The sale spans toolkits for Photoshop, Illustrator, Procreate, Clip Studio, and Affinity. Check the app version before you buy, then put some actual grit into those style frames.

Preview True Grit’s Black Friday Sale

Sale pricing starts with the event. Check product/app compatibility and the asset license for your use. End date and coupon details have not been published.

Offer & terms

Fab

Up to 70% off selected assets and tools through December 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Start an Unreal Engine shot with a ready-made environment, or pick up a sky or water system instead of building one for a single scene. Filter by your engine or file format before you start browsing.

Browse The Fab Friday Mega Sale

Discounts vary by listing. Check the license tier and engine version before buying.

Sale announcement

ActionVFX

40% off the entire store for 40 hours.

Need smoke, sparks, or a dust hit to sell a comp? Start with the clips your shot actually calls for, then compare angles and lighting before you buy.

Build Your ActionVFX Wishlist

The vendor has not published a promo code or subscription renewal terms for this sale.

Offer & terms

Motion Ape

33% off MoBar Lifetime, MoPack, and Doodles.

Put your most-used After Effects commands on a custom MoBar panel, or reach for MoPack and Doodles when you need quick transitions or hand-drawn accents.

Shop The Motion Ape Sale

MoBar savings apply to the Lifetime license. Use the sale links on the campaign page.

Offer & terms

Krotos

Up to 80% off select sound design tools.

Build sound around the cut instead of auditioning fifty nearly identical whooshes. Krotos Studio lets you shape sounds to picture, while Reformer Pro is useful when you want to perform and layer Foley.

Shop Krotos Sound Design Tools

Studio Pro and Max discounts are for the first year on annual billing and renew at standard rates. Select plug-ins are one-time purchases; check pricing for your region.

Offer & terms

Topaz Labs

Studio Collection annual plan: $299 instead of $499.

If an edit depends on a soft archive shot or a noisy plate, Topaz can help you test whether the footage is worth keeping. Preview a few seconds at delivery resolution before processing the whole sequence.

Shop Topaz Black Friday Pricing

The quoted price is for the annual Studio Collection plan. Check commercial licensing, cloud credits, and renewal pricing for the plan you choose.

Offer & terms

Sonniss

Up to 60% off independent sound effects libraries.

Find UI ticks, Foley, or room tone to make your animation feel like it lives somewhere. Audition a focused pack before springing for a giant bundle you may spend more time tagging than using.

Browse The Sonniss Sound Effects Sale

Prices are in US dollars. Library licenses cover commercial use without a subscription.

Offer & terms

A Sound Effect

Black November discounts on select audio tools and libraries, plus a free library with orders of $59 or more.

Give a UI animation its own vocabulary of clicks, alerts, and transitions. Browse the independent libraries by project need, and check the deadline on each flash deal before building your cart.

Browse Black November Sound Effects

The free-library selection depends on order value. Discounts vary by publisher and library.

Offer & terms

ElevenLabs

Creator annual plan for $99 (55% off); 55% off annual Pro for new Pro subscribers, or 50% off when switching from monthly Pro.

Test voiceover timing before you lock an explainer animatic. For client-facing work, check the voice rights and plan terms before using generated audio in the final cut.

View ElevenLabs Annual Plan Offers

Eligible annual plans only. Pro savings depend on whether you are new to Pro or switching from monthly.

Offer & terms

Clam Sync

25% off the Solo license.

If your motion project includes interviews or multicam footage, sync cameras and separately recorded audio before you start designing around the edit. Try the free version with your footage and editor first.

Shop The Clam Sync Solo Deal

Solo is a one-time purchase with one year of updates. Future updates are optional and priced separately.

Offer & terms

FX Elements

70% off individual FX Clips and 50% off FX Packs.

Add drifting fog or falling snow to a comp without building a particle sim. Buy a single clip for a specific shot, or pick up a pack when you need matching variations across a sequence.

Shop The FX Elements Black Friday Sale

The 70% discount is for individual clips, not packs. Another deal is scheduled to unlock November 23.

Offer & terms

Toolfarm

Black Friday and year-end savings on motion design, VFX, and audio software.

Toolfarm’s sale is a good place to compare tools across your workflow. Start with the plug-ins you already know you’ll use, like an easing tool for After Effects or a flare pack for your next comp. The bigger discounts don’t all start on the same day.

Browse Toolfarm’s Black Friday Deals

Mt. Mograph: 20% off all products through November 25, then 35% off November 27–30, 2026. Both offers include the Ultimate Bundle.

Video Copilot: Save 40% November 25–December 2, 2026, including on Element 3D and Optical Flares.

DaVinci Resolve Studio: Save 20% through November 20, 2026. This offer ends earlier than the others.

Native Instruments Massive XL: 50% off introductory pricing. Check the current offer and deadline on Toolfarm’s product page.

HDRI Hub

50% off everything with code BLACK50.

Try a few lighting moods on the same product render without rebuilding the rig. HDRI Hub has skies, interiors and studio-style light maps you can use to change the reflections and overall light in your scene.

Shop HDRI Hub’s Lighting Maps

Check the format and resolution on the asset page before buying; the store offers HDR and EXR maps in different sizes.

Offer & terms

Caddis

Caddis 1.x export license for $99 instead of $129.

Try a browser-based motion tool on your next animated title or looping graphic. You can build and preview for free, then decide whether the one-time export license is worth it for your workflow.

See The Caddis Export License Deal

The one-time license covers Caddis 1.x on two devices and includes unlimited exports. No subscription.

Offer & terms

Blendkit

33% off the Full Plan and eligible Blender add-ons.

Block a 3D scene with ready-made props and materials so you can spend more time on lighting and camera moves. Check the free library first; the Full Plan unlocks the full catalog.

See The Blendkit Sale And Eligible Add-Ons

The discounted Full Plan rate carries over only while auto-renewal stays on. The add-on discount applies to the sale selection.

Offer & terms

Kstudio

30% or more off featured 3ds Max tools and digital assets.

If finding the right model or material takes longer than placing it, start with Project Manager. It lets you browse your asset library inside 3ds Max instead of digging through folders mid-scene.

Shop Kstudio’s Black Friday Deals

Savings vary by product. Check version compatibility and what’s included before buying a plugin or bundle.

Offer & terms

Spline Dynamics

30% off all Spline Dynamics 3ds Max plugins with code BLACK30.

For a shot that needs repeated objects, clean splines, or forms built along paths, start with the tool that solves the problem you actually have. Spline Dynamics makes dedicated 3ds Max plugins for tasks such as scattering and spline cleanup.

Browse Spline Dynamics Plugins

The offer applies to its 3ds Max plugins; check the product page for compatibility with your version.

Offer & terms

RUVAU

FaceTweak for $39 USD, down from $69.

Fix a distracting eyeline or make a small mouth-shape adjustment without sending the shot out of the edit. Try it on your own footage or animated character before buying, especially if the shot has fast movement.

Get The FaceTweak Black Friday Deal

One-time license for two active computers. Works in DaVinci Resolve Free and Studio and in Premiere Pro; processing is local.

Offer & terms

Soundtoys

Up to 75% off individual effects; Soundtoys 5 is $239, down from $599.

Turn a clean click or synth note into a textured transition with delay, saturation or reverb. If one effect solves the job, price it separately before springing for the whole bundle.

Shop Soundtoys Black Friday Deals

The $239 price is for the standard Soundtoys 5 bundle. Academic and account-specific upgrade offers are separate.

Offer & terms

Render Camp

Up to 91% off recorded 3D visualization training bundles.

Practice taking a raw 3D scene through materials, lighting and a finished render. The bundles focus on interiors and exteriors, so they’re a good fit if you want to improve the environments behind your motion work.

See Render Camp’s Black Friday Bundles

Includes one year of access to recordings, not live feedback or a diploma. The biggest discount is on the largest bundle. Payments from Russia and Belarus are not accepted.

Offer & terms

The Pixel Lab

30% off the entire store with code FALL30.

Grab a VDB for an atmospheric shot or a material pack for a render you need to finish this week. Browse by renderer before checking out so you don’t buy a pack built for a different pipeline.

Shop The Pixel Lab’s Black Friday Sale

Check the product page for host-app and renderer compatibility. The store does not list a cutoff on the sale banner.

Offer & terms

Reallusion

50% off eligible Content Store assets from November 20 through November 30, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

Block a character shot with stock motion, then spend your time on the performance instead of building every walk cycle from scratch. The sale covers assets for iClone, Character Creator, and Cartoon Animator.

Shop Reallusion’s Content Store Sale

The discount is off list prices. Mega Bundles, items already discounted by 50% or more, and purchases outside the Content Store are excluded. Other product coupons do not stack, except the eligible PRIME coupon. Content Store purchases are nonrefundable.

Offer & terms

Soft8Soft: Verge3D

25% off the Soft8Soft store through November 30, 2026, with code BlackFriday.

Turn a product render into something a client can actually spin and explore in a browser. Verge3D works with Blender, 3ds Max, and Maya, and its visual scripting tools let you wire up interactions without writing them from scratch.

Shop The Verge3D sale

Choose the license and edition that match your team size and 3D app. The discount also applies to material packs.

Brand announcement

Magic Automa AI

40% off Studio, Studio Max, and eligible upgrades through November 30, 2026, with code BLACKFRIDAY2026.

If every client revision starts with the same layer or export chores, turn that sequence into one reusable macro. The tool supports tasks such as replacing footage in After Effects or adding review markers in DaVinci Resolve.

Compare Magic Automa Plans

Paid licenses are one-time purchases and include updates within the current major version. AI macro generation requires an internet connection. Runs on Windows 10+ and macOS 15+.

License details

iMeshh

40% off the first six months of monthly Lite and Pro plans, or the first year on annual plans. The offer ends November 30, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. UK time.

Dress a Blender set with ready-made furniture, materials, and lighting assets. Lite includes the full library, so compare the plans before paying for studio features you may not need.

Compare iMeshh’s Black Friday Plans

The regular price resumes after the discounted period. The offer page shows pricing in GBP, USD, and EUR.

Offer & terms

StormVFX: HydroFX

25% off HydroFX Indie and Studio annual plans with code BLACKFRIDAY2026.

Build a product splash or a foamy wave in a standalone water simulator, then export the cache back into your 3D pipeline. HydroFX can use imported geometry as emitters or colliders.

Get The HydroFX Black Friday Deal

Requires Windows and an NVIDIA CUDA GPU. The vendor’s checkout shows annual billing but does not confirm whether the discount carries over at renewal.

Offer & terms

Next Limit

Up to 50% off eligible RealFlow and Maxwell licenses through December 3, 2026.

Use RealFlow to simulate the liquid in a product shot, or Maxwell to render the final still or animation. They are separate tools, so start with the part of the job you actually need help with.

Shop Next Limit’s RealFlow Sale

RealFlow for Cinema 4D starts at €347.50 and Maxwell Studio at €247.50. Check host-app compatibility and confirm the license configuration before checkout.

Maxwell offers

3DModels.org

Up to 80% off selected 3D models in the Black Friday sale.

Need a vehicle for a pitch frame or background shot? Start with a downloadable model and spend the time you saved on lighting and camera movement.

Browse Discounted 3D Models

Discounts vary by model. Check the included file formats and license before buying.

Sale announcement

Hardware Deals For Motion Designers

Pen displays, computers, and graphics cards for building out your setup. These are U.S. prices checked November 19, 2026; confirm current price and availability before buying.

Huion Kamvas 13 (Gen 3)

$199 at Huion ($50 off) through November 30. See Huion’s sale terms.

A compact 13.3-inch pen display for sketching storyboards, drawing assets, and animating frame by frame. It connects to your computer; it’s not a standalone tablet.

Shop The Kamvas 13

Huion Kamvas 16 (Gen 3)

$419 at Huion ($80 off) through November 30. See Huion’s sale terms.

If your toolbars keep crowding your drawing, the 15.8-inch, 2.5K display gives you more space for a style frame or a full storyboard panel. Like the 13, it connects to your computer.

Shop The Kamvas 16

MSI Vector 16 HX AI

$1,599 at Newegg ($400 off the listed comparison price).

The RTX 5070 Ti laptop GPU is the draw if you need CUDA rendering away from your desk. This build comes with 16 GB of system RAM and a 512 GB SSD, so budget for more memory and storage if you regularly juggle heavy comps, textures, and caches.

See The MSI Vector At Newegg

HP HyperX OMEN MAX 45L

$2,889.99 at HP ($1,070 off the listed MSRP).

A configurable desktop to compare if you want one machine for compositing and 3D. Check the GPU, RAM, and storage in the configurator before buying: the price can change with your selections. Even at the advertised discount, it’s worth comparing against similarly equipped PCs.

Configure The OMEN MAX 45L

ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 XT

$1,079.99 at Newegg ($65 off the listed comparison price).

This 16 GB card is an option if your renderer supports AMD GPUs. Check compatibility before buying, especially if your workflow depends on CUDA. At about 5% off, this is a price to compare, not a reason to rush.

Check The Radeon Price At Newegg

PNY GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Overclocked

$1,479.99 in Best Buy’s listing ($20 below the displayed prior price). See the exact PNY model.

The 16 GB of VRAM and CUDA support are useful for GPU rendering, but $20 is a small markdown on a card at this price. Compare other 5070 Ti listings before you commit.

Compare RTX 5070 Ti Prices At Best Buy

Wacom

Holiday sale announced. Eligible models and U.S. pricing are still to come.

If you’re comparing a pen tablet or display for drawing assets and roughing out animation, keep an eye on Wacom’s eStore before you choose a model.

Check Wacom’s U.S. Sales Page

We’re waiting for Wacom to confirm which U.S. models are included and what they’ll cost.

Sale announcement

Miscellaneous

UPLIFT V3 Essential Standing Desk

From $399, down from $469 ($70 off).

Change working height between sketching at a pen display and reviewing a cut. Check the desktop dimensions against the gear you actually keep on your desk.

Shop The V3 Essential Standing Desk

The separate BF2026 sale offers $100 off orders of $999+ through November 29. That threshold is above the price of this desk alone.

Offer & terms

Elgato Stream Deck MK.2

$119.99, down from $149.99 ($30 off).

Put repetitive After Effects actions on dedicated keys: trim a layer, tap a marker, or launch a script without hunting through menus.

Shop Elgato’s Stream Deck Deal

This is the 15-key Stream Deck MK.2. The Black Friday page lists other models and bundles separately.

Product details

Huanuo Monitor Arm With Laptop Tray

$37.98 at Amazon.

Lift your monitor and laptop off the work surface to make space for a pen display or sketchbook.

See The Huanuo Arm At Amazon

Fits 13–32-inch VESA monitors up to 22 lb. Check your monitor’s mount pattern and desk clamp clearance.

Product details

Logitech MX Master 3S

$79.99 at Amazon, down from $99.99 as reported by PCWorld.

Use the thumb wheel to move sideways through a long timeline, or assign the programmable buttons to actions you repeat all day.

Shop The MX Master 3S At Amazon

This listing is the graphite Bluetooth version without a USB receiver.

entry.summary: The Future of Motion Design: Live Talk from AEPDX 2025 In this keynote from Portland, Joey explores "The Futurey Feeling" - that sensation when you recognize the next big shift in motion design before everyone else catches on. Drawing from 25+ years in the industry, Joey breaks d
entry.content:
The Future of Motion Design: Live Talk from AEPDX 2025

In this keynote from Portland, Joey explores "The Futurey Feeling" - that sensation when you recognize the next big shift in motion design before everyone else catches on. Drawing from 25+ years in the industry, Joey breaks down three massive technological shifts happening right now:

By Joey Korenman5 min readAdMiCh

Have you ever had that feeling when you see a new technology and just know it's going to change everything? That moment when you recognize the future before everyone else catches on? Joey Korenman calls this "The Futurey Feeling" – and if you're a motion designer, you need to pay attention to it.

In this keynote presentation from Portland, OR's AEPDX event, Joey draws from over 25 years in the motion design industry to identify three massive technological shifts happening right now. These aren't just incremental improvements – they're paradigm changes that will define the next decade of our industry.

The Pattern of Disruption

Before diving into the current wave, Joey takes us back through history to show a consistent pattern. From the desktop editing revolution that killed traditional post houses to the rise of CGI that transformed filmmaking, technological disruption follows a predictable cycle:

  1. Resistance - Industry veterans dismiss the new technology as inferior

  2. Gradual adoption - Early adopters start proving the technology's worth

  3. Explosive growth - Demand skyrockets as barriers drop (Jevons Paradox in action)

  4. New opportunities - More work emerges than ever existed before

The key insight? Every time technology makes something easier and cheaper, demand explodes rather than shrinks.

The Three Current Waves

1. Real-Time 3D Rendering

We're witnessing the democratization of real-time 3D engines like Unreal Engine. This isn't just about faster renders – it's about entirely new possibilities:

  • Feature films rendered entirely in real-time (like the Oscar-nominated film rendered on the director's home PC)

  • Live concert visuals that respond dynamically to the performance (Phish at the Sphere)

  • Virtual production shoots getting 8+ locations in a day instead of 2-3

  • Real-time client sessions for 3D work, just like we do with editing

The technology exists today. Most clients don't know it's possible yet. That's your opportunity.

2. Interactive Animation Revolution

The second wave is already transforming how we create animation for apps and websites. Tools like Rive are eliminating the painful translation process between After Effects and code:

  • Direct handoff from motion designer to developer

  • Responsive design built into animation workflows

  • Real-time interactivity without complex development

  • Massive market expansion beyond traditional motion design

Companies like Duolingo are already building entire studios around this workflow, acquiring traditional motion design shops to fuel their app experiences.

3. AI as a Creative Accelerator

The third wave is the most controversial but potentially most transformative. AI isn't replacing motion designers – it's giving them superpowers:

  • Asset generation on demand instead of hunting through stock libraries

  • Visual ideation that accelerates the creative process

  • Technical problem solving for tasks that used to require specialists

  • Rapid prototyping of concepts that would be too expensive to test traditionally

The key is understanding AI as a tool for making the impossible possible within budget and deadline constraints.

Why This Matters Now

We're at an inflection point. The motion design industry just emerged from a challenging couple of years, but leading indicators suggest we're entering a growth phase. The studios and freelancers who understand these technological shifts – and can educate their clients about new possibilities – will capture disproportionate value.

The opportunity isn't just in using these tools. It's in being the person who shows clients what's suddenly possible.

Your Next Steps

You don't need to master all three areas immediately. Pick the one that resonates most and start experimenting:

  • For real-time 3D: Download Unreal Engine and start with basic scene creation

  • For interactive animation: Try Rive for your next web or app project

  • For AI integration: Experiment with Midjourney for asset creation or ChatGPT for ideation

The goal isn't perfection – it's awareness. When you spot an opportunity that matches one of these capabilities, you'll be ready to act.

The Futurey Feeling in Action

Joey's message is ultimately optimistic. Yes, technological change can feel threatening. But history shows us that making creative work easier and more accessible creates exponentially more opportunities, not fewer.

The motion designers who thrive in the next decade won't be the ones who resist change – they'll be the ones who embrace it early, educate their clients about new possibilities, and ride the wave of expanded demand.

Are you feeling futurey yet?

entry.content:
Why Houdini's Procedural Workflow Is Changing Motion Graphics Forever

Discover the power of procedural workflows in Houdini and learn how they can transform your motion graphics process.

By Nick Donatelli2 min read

If you've been keeping an eye on the motion design industry, you've probably noticed Houdini making waves...

What was once considered primarily a VFX tool for Hollywood blockbusters is now becoming an increasingly popular choice for motion designers. But why? The answer lies in one powerful concept: proceduralism.

In our latest tutorial, motion designer Nick Donatelli breaks down what makes Houdini's procedural workflow so revolutionary for motion graphics artists. Whether you're curious about making the switch or just want to understand what all the buzz is about, this tutorial offers an accessible introduction to one of the most powerful tools in modern motion design.

✨ What Is Proceduralism?

At its core, proceduralism is a method of working where you build tools instead of assets. Every change you make is saved as part of a flexible system, giving you the ability to iterate on ideas without committing to a specific look. Think of it as the difference between painting directly on a canvas versus building a machine that can paint infinite variations of your vision.

In the tutorial, Nick demonstrates this concept beautifully by showing how a simple change to parameters like size, count, or angle can dynamically adapt an entire model - and even the animation automatically updates to match. This kind of flexibility is a game-changer when you're working on real-world projects with tight deadlines and clients who love to request "just one more revision."

⚡️ The Power of Non-Destructive Workflows

One of Houdini's greatest strengths is its non-destructive, node-based workflow. Unlike traditional 3D applications where changes often mean starting over or carefully working backwards through your history, Houdini's nodes can be rearranged, disabled, or modified at any point without destroying your work.

Nick shows how you can experiment with completely different looks by simply rearranging nodes, all while never permanently altering your geometry. Want to add scales to a dragon model? No problem - and if you change your mind about the scale size, distribution, or style later, those changes ripple through your entire setup automatically.

🔄 Why Motion Designers Are Making The Switch

The motion graphics industry moves fast, and client revisions are inevitable. Houdini's procedural approach means you can accommodate those changes without rebuilding from scratch. It's not just about efficiency - it's about creative freedom. When you know you can easily iterate, you're more likely to experiment and push your designs further.

While there's definitely a learning curve (Houdini's interface can be intimidating at first), the payoff is enormous. The ability to create flexible, parametric systems that can be adjusted on the fly is increasingly valuable in modern motion design workflows.

👀 Ready to Explore Houdini?

If this tutorial has piqued your interest in procedural workflows, you're not alone. More and more motion designers are discovering the power of tools like Houdini to expand their creative capabilities. And while you're leveling up your skills, don't forget that School of Motion's All Access program offers comprehensive training across the entire motion design ecosystem - from Cinema 4D and Blender to After Effects and Unreal Engine.

Watch the full tutorial above to see these concepts in action, and let us know in the comments: Are you using Houdini in your workflow? What made you curious about procedural techniques? We'd love to hear about your journey!

entry.content:
How to Achieve Your Goals and Make All Your Dreams Come True

Struggling to stick to your creative goals? Learn practical methods for setting targets, tracking ideas, and staying motivated on your artistic journey.

By Nick Greenawalt5 min read

Want a foolproof way to set goals, stay motivated, and achieve everything you want?

Do you struggle with sticking to your creative goals? Want a tried-and-true method of tracking ideas, staying creative, and achieving your dreams? Well, all that might be overpromising, but we do have some excellent tips that you can use right now to start making actual progress on your artistic journey.

One of the most challenging things about being an artist is self-motivation. Without some big mean boss staring over your shoulder, it's easy to get distracted by the Internet or TV or existential dread. Fortunately, I've been pushing myself to be more consistent in my creation for years, and I've learned some invaluable tips that I can't wait to share.

In this video, I want to break down some methods I’ve learned over the years on how to achieve your goals and make your dreams come true.

  • Setting Goals

  • Tracking Your Ideas

  • Taking Action

How to Achieve Your Goals and Make All Your Dreams Come True

How to Set Goals as an Artist

So let’s talk about your goals.

What do you want to achieve? And how can you get there? How do you know what you want to achieve? For me, this didn’t become clear until I actually wrote my goals down.

When you're setting goals, you can look to your peers and idols for inspiration. Identify the path you're trying to walk so you at least know which direction to head. Once you have an idea of a goal, it's time to break it down into short and long term targets.

Your long term goals need to be big. If you're on a hike, you're not going to use some small pebble in the distance as a marker; you use a mountain. At the same time, you need to break down your goals into smaller milestones that lead you toward them. I like to set up daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly goals. Each one supports the next, taking me closer to where I want to be.

Don’t underestimate the power of writing. There is something scientifically magical about writing, because while you are writing, while your hand is connected to the paper, your brain is physically not able to focus on anything else. This is according to a scientific study that I made up right now.

How to Track Your Creative Ideas

So let’s try an exercise. All you need is some blank wall space and some post it notes. If you don’t have any post it’s, feel free to write directly on the wall.?

First, let's make a big goal. What is it you want to accomplish this year? Maybe you want to buy a car, or get a new job. When I first did this exercise, my year goal was to go freelance, so that’s going to be my goal here.

Now let's fill in some shorter term goals. This month, I want to make a new YouTube video (check and check).

This week, I need to engage with clients and finish storyboards for my next video. Today, that means I'm reviewing potential leads and sketching my boards.

Your short term goals are smaller segments of the larger goals. By doing your daily tasks, you chip away at the weekly and monthly targets.

It's also important that these goals are actionable—not vague. For example, don’t write “get more clients.” Instead try “get 1 freelance project next month.” As James Clear said, "When making plans, think big. When making progress, think small."

Finally, we're using Post-Its because—sadly—sometimes you won't hit your goals. That's okay! Just move that note down and hit it next time.

Taking Action On Your Creative Projects

Okay so you have some goals, but how do you actually *achieve* them? Well I already told you the scientific importance of writing stuff down. And if you think I’m joking, I want to show you how serious I am.

I keep a notebook in every single room of my house, because my memory is not good and I don’t want to lose any ideas that might come to me: in my office, in my kitchen, in my car, even in my shower. Write down all your ideas, no matter the quality. Keep them synced on a Google Doc. No matter how dumb or insignificant you think it might be, write it down. You never know when you might come back to them and days, weeks, months, or years later one of those dumb ideas might turn into something brilliant.

Now just writing down ideas, of course, isn’t enough. You have to do them. But you are creative, smart, and amazing. So that’s the easy part. The hard part as creatives is putting your stuff—and yourself—out there. This is also the most important part, because if you don’t put yourself out there, no one else is going to find you.

You never know where an opportunity might lead. If you think an idea is good, other people are going to think that idea is good too. The things that you make out of passion, or because you had an idea that you just had to go after, are the things that will have the biggest impact on your career and life. Don’t be afraid of failure / failure is a good thing / if you aren't constantly failing you. No one gets it right on the first try, they have just failed enough times to figure it out that time.

Not everyone is going to like your stuff - and that's okay. There are people who don't like pizza. If there are people who don’t like pizza then you cannot please everyone so there’s no point in trying. Make the things you want to make.

This is a marathon, not a sprint, and the only way you'll fail is if you quit.

Need Help Deciding Your Next Big Goal?

We hope that tutorial pumped you up for your next big project. What are you going to work on next? Where is your career headed? Are you still unsure? Well, maybe we can help out even more. It's time to Level Up.

In Level Up, you’ll explore the ever-expanding field of Motion Design, discovering where you fit in and where you’re going next. By the end of this course, you’ll have a roadmap to help you get to the next level of your Motion Design career.
